newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's 30 top groups agree to freeze 1997 wages.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's 30 top groups agree to freeze 1997 wages.

text.p: South Korea's 30 leading business conglomerates said on Wednesday they agreed to freeze wage payments for 1997 at last year's level.
"Wage freeze is necessary to strengthen international competitiveness," said an official at the Federation of Korean Industries, the lobbying body for the nation's major companies.
Senior officials of the nation's 30 largest business groups, called chaebol, also said they opposed the legalisation of the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions.
They also demanded that employers be allowed to lay off workers and manage working hours flexibly, opposing the opposition parties' draft revision of a controversial labour law.
The bill, proposed by opposition parties, supported repealing a clause that allows worker layoffs and recognising the confederation.
On Tuesday the confederation, which claims 500,000 member workers nation-wide, said it would launch an all-out strike on Friday unless a controversial new labour law was repealed.
They vowed to deter the new law from taking effect from March 1 by going on strike.
The confederation earlier said it would decide when to order its member unions to walk out after a televised address by President Kim Young-sam on Tuesday.

Kim apologised over the labour law rammed through parliament last December, but fell short of satisfying the union, which demanded the revoke of the law that makes it easier for employers to lay off workers and replace strikers.
Union leaders said they would also look for more positive results from parliamentary debates which reopened last week.
Ruling and opposition parties are discussing possible revision of the law in a labour committee.
The National Assembly reopened on February 17 for a 30-day session to discuss the labour law and probe into the Hanbo scandal.
The ruling New Korea party passed the law in parliament in late December while opposition members slept, triggering almost a month of strikes.
